Records.description: One-loop massless pentagon topology for five-particle scattering. 11 master integrals computed through $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2)$ in terms of pentagon functions (MPLs).

Massless one-loop 5-point pentagon integral family used for computing 5-gluon helicity amplitudes via the intersection theory / dual form formalism. In the massless degeneration, the basis shrinks from 31 (generic masses) to 11 master integrals: 5 bubbles, 5 one-mass boxes (reorganized as finite 6-dimensional boxes), and 1 pentagon (which vanishes at $d=4$). The paper computes all generalized unitarity coefficients to all orders in epsilon for all independent helicity configurations. Ancillary files contain the full epsilon-dependent results in momentum twistor parametrization.

Records.description: One-loop scalar pentagon with 5 massless propagators and 5 on-shell massless external legs. Main result: one-fold integral representation exact in $d$. Epsilon expansion near $d=6$ yields Goncharov polylogarithms. $Z_5$ cyclic symmetry. 11 MIs (1 pentagon + 5 boxes + 5 bubbles).

One-loop massless pentagon with five massless external legs and five massless internal propagators. The spanning set of cuts up to symmetry is $\{\{z_4,z_5\}, \{z_3,z_5\}\}$. Diagonal bases are given for each cut. On the $\{z_3,z_5\}$ cut, the basis requires an extra element '1' (no propagator poles), indicating that the diagonal basis prescription sometimes needs modifications for massless kinematics.
One-loop one-mass pentagon. 5 massless propagators. 13 MIs ($\sigma_{id}$). Part of 856-function pentagon function basis with 156-letter $S_4$ alphabet.

Records.authors: Caron-Huot, Simon, Giroux, Mathieu, Hannesdottir, Holmfridur S., Mizera, Sebastian
Records.description: Massless one-loop pentagon family with 5 external massless legs. Used to verify crossing conjecture for all one-loop five-point master integrals via canonical differential equations. 11 master integrals: 5 bubbles, 5 one-mass boxes, and 1 pentagon in $D=6-2\varepsilon$.

Fully massless one-loop pentagon in $D = 6 - 2\varepsilon$ dimensions, five cyclic Mandelstam invariants $s_i = (q_i - q_{i+2})^2$. The paper gives closed-form results for all cuts required by the diagrammatic coaction: the order-$\varepsilon^1$ maximal cut is $\ln(-16 \, \mathrm{Gram}_5 / (s_1 s_2 s_3 s_4 s_5))$; the order-$\varepsilon^0$ quadruple cut (all propagators but $i$ on shell) is $\ln(\bar{v}/v)$ where $v$ and $\bar{v}$ are square roots of $16 \, \mathrm{Gram}_5$ shifted by the cyclic polynomial in the $s_i$; all triple cuts vanish. Substituting these into the generic pentagon DE reproduces the known Kozlov-Lee differential equation and the symbol letters match a subset of those appearing in two-loop five-point massless integrals.

One-loop pentagon with 3m; 3 off-shell external legs $(q_1,q_3,q_5)$ with SDE $x$-parametrization, labelled family $E$ in the paper. 18 masters solved via SDE approach with $x$-parametrization rationalizing square roots; canonical DE; Goncharov polylogs up to weight 4. Called $E$ in the paper.

Records.description: Massless one-loop pentagon, the simplest case where evanescent integrals arise. Ten IR regions (five soft, five collinear) are identified. Within 166 UV-compatible monomials at rank five, 141 are locally finite with six rank-two generators, and 40 are evanescent with the evanescent sub-ideal generated by the out-of-plane component squared.

Records.description: One-loop pentagon master-integral family with one massive leg (the operator momentum q = p1+p2+p3+p4 with q^2 != 0) and four on-shell massless external momenta p_i^2=0. Used in the IBP reduction of the one-loop and two-loop four-point form factor of the stress-tensor supermultiplet tr(phi_{12}^2) in planar N=4 SYM. The UT one-loop pentagon I^{(1)}_{Pen}(i,j,k,l) is multiplied by 4i*epsilon(1234)*mu_{ll}, contributes the parity-odd piece of the form factor at O(eps), and is part of the basis from Abreu:2020jxa, Canko:2020ylt. Propagator list given in PropList[(*P*)] of anc/2_UT_Masters_Definition.m.

Records.description: $n$-gon family, ngon_L5_massless. The one-loop $n$-gon (or $A_n$ polygon) has $n$ massless internal propagators arranged in a cycle with $n$ massless external legs. In $D = n$ dimensions the integral is finite and evaluates to the volume of a hyperbolic $(n{-}1)$-simplex (Davydychev-Delbourgo 1997). For $n = 3$ (triangle) the result involves Clausen functions; for $n = 4$ (box) it is the Murakami-Yano formula in 16 dilogarithms. The family includes the bubble ($n = 2$), triangle, box, pentagon, hexagon, heptagon, and octagon.
